summary: Static inspection of the bridge tests, bridge implementation, authentication rollout helper, and integration contract identified an existing no-repost boundary assertion and a missing parent-scope rejection case in the inspected test file. The four inspected files match their manifest digests. No tests were run; these observations do not establish live isolation or delivery.

observations.claim: Existing boundary: an uncertain issue-creation POST must not be automatically repeated.
observations.symbol: never reposts an uncertain request, and links only an exact observed candidate
observations.evidence: At lines 131-141, api(record).state.failPost is set to true. The first operate(..., { command: "submit", token: TOKEN }, ...) must reject with "POST outcome unknown"; the second must reject with "never repost". After rejecting a candidate with a changed description and linking the exact candidate, expect(a.posts()).toHaveLength(1) requires only one POST attempt across the sequence. These assertions would catch a retry that sends another issue-creation request after losing the first response, risking duplicate execution even if the first request reached the server. source/scripts/paperclip-bridge/bridge.ts operate, lines 207-221, enforces this through the pre-POST journal and unknown-outcome refusal. source/docs/paperclip-integration.md, lines 28-38, specifies observation and exact linking instead of automatic resend. This describes the assertions and source, not a test execution result.

observations.claim: Plausible remaining regression gap: parent-scoped bridge keys are rejected in source but lack a rejection case in the inspected bridge test file.
observations.evidence: assertIsolation at lines 128-140 rejects a truthy scope.parentIssueId or nonempty scope.parentIssueIds, and operate calls it before issue creation at line 199. The "refuses %s authority before POST" matrix in source/tests/paperclip-bridge.test.ts, lines 166-175, covers anonymous access, standard scope, wrong company/project, extra projects, and extra assignees; neither it nor the remaining tests in that file supplies a parent scope. A concrete additional case would retain the valid api(record) fixture but set a.state.me.keyScope.parentIssueId to "10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005", then call submit on the committed record. It should reject with "requires a task_bridge key for exactly this project and assignee" and leave a.posts() equal to []. Removing the parentIssueId check could otherwise allow this input to reach an issue-creation POST without the existing matrix detecting that regression. A companion case can set parentIssueIds to an array containing the same UUID. The exact project/assignee requirement is described in source/docs/paperclip-integration.md, lines 72-74. The current implementation already rejects these inputs; this is a bounded test-coverage observation, not an observed authorization defect or a claim about all repository tests.
